title: Securitization, ABS CDOs, and the 2007 Credit Meltdown
targetAudience: Quantitative Finance Students & Professional Risk Managers
learningObjectives: Understand the mechanics of the origin-to-distribute model and SPV waterfall distribution.
Deconstruct credit subordination across Senior (AAA), Mezzanine (BBB), and Equity tranches.
Analyze the ABS CDO structure and understand how financial alchemy repackaged BBB risk into AAA debt.
Trace the subprime crisis roots: teaser rates, NINJA loans, and originator-investor agency conflicts.
Evaluate default correlation breakdown and calculate exact tranche wipeout losses.
Examine post-crisis reforms under Basel III and Dodd-Frank skin-in-the-game risk retention.

pedagogicalPillars.title: The Waterfall Architecture
pedagogicalPillars.concept: Cash flows and losses are distributed in strict hierarchical priority, subordinating lower tranches.

pedagogicalPillars.title: The ABS CDO Multiplier
pedagogicalPillars.concept: Repackaging BBB tranches into secondary CDOs magnified sensitivity to housing market default correlations.

pedagogicalPillars.title: Mathematical Wipeout Dynamics
pedagogicalPillars.concept: Collateral losses exceed equity cushions rapidly, causing catastrophic total losses in mezzanine and CDO tranches.

pedagogicalPillars.title: Institutional & Regulatory Redesign
pedagogicalPillars.concept: Basel III capital buffers and Dodd-Frank 5% skin-in-the-game mandates re-align originators with investors.

misconceptions.misconception: AAA credit rating means an ABS tranche is completely immune to mortgage defaults.
misconceptions.rebuttal: AAA indicates minimal risk under normal historical conditions; in an ABS CDO, a modest 10% collateral default rate across underlying pools can wipe out even AAA senior tranches entirely.

misconceptions.misconception: Diversification across US states protects against mortgage portfolio defaults.
misconceptions.rebuttal: Diversification only works when regional risks are uncorrelated; when national home prices fall simultaneously, default correlations jump to 1.0.

activeRecallChallenge.scenario: An ABS holds $100M in subprime mortgages structured into 80% Senior (AAA), 15% Mezzanine (BBB), and 5% Equity tranches. Nationwide housing defaults cause total collateral losses of 14% on the portfolio ($14M loss). How much loss is absorbed by each tranche?
activeRecallChallenge.question: What is the net dollar loss suffered by the Mezzanine tranche?
options: $9 Million loss (Equity absorbs first $5M, Mezzanine absorbs remaining $9M out of $15M, Senior takes $0)
$14 Million loss (Mezzanine absorbs the entire $14M portfolio loss)
$5 Million loss (Mezzanine loss is capped at $5M)
$0 loss (The AAA Senior tranche absorbs all losses first)
activeRecallChallenge.detailedExplanation: Under the bottom-up loss waterfall, the 5% Equity tranche ($5M) absorbs the first $5M of losses and is 100% wiped out. The remaining $9M of loss ($14M - $5M) is absorbed entirely by the 15% Mezzanine tranche ($15M principal), leaving it with $6M residual value (a 60% loss). The 80% Senior tranche takes $0 loss because cumulative losses (14%) did not breach the 20% subordination attachment point.
